member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Agents.ChildProcessJob
member.summary: A Windows job object for ONE child process and everything it spawns, created with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE. kills the whole tree atomically (including grandchildren started a moment before the kill), and if the host (AutoCAD) exits or crashes, Windows closes the handle and kills the tree too. No-op on other operating systems; failures are logged and the caller falls back to Process.Kill(entireProcessTree).

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases
member.summary: Command aliases and external (operating-system) commands, as defined by acad.pgp. holds the aliases of the default acad.pgp that matter to ; adds the user's own file so a custom alias of a blocked command (for example XX,*SHELL) and every external command (DEL, DEL, 8, File to delete: ,) are caught too. Immutable and thread-safe.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases.Default
member.summary: The built-in aliases (default acad.pgp entries that lead to blocked, approval or dialog commands).

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases.AliasCount
member.summary: Number of aliases known.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases.ExternalCommandCount
member.summary: Number of external (operating-system) commands known from the pgp file.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases.FromPgp(System.String)
member.summary: The built-in aliases plus every alias and external command defined in (the text of acad.pgp). Lines starting with ';' are comments. Aliases are NAME,*COMMAND; external commands are NAME,[OS command],flags,[*]prompt,. Entries of the file win over the built-in ones.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases.Resolve(System.String)
member.summary: The command an alias stands for (it may start with '-', e.g. "LO" -> "-LAYOUT"), or null when is not an alias. is upper case without the prefixes _ . + ' (a leading '-' is part of the alias: "-LA" -> "-LAYER").

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases.IsExternalCommand(System.String)
member.summary: True when is an external (operating-system) command of the pgp file.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText
member.summary: Pure helpers that read AutoCAD's command-line text (English AutoCAD): which history lines are new after an input, which are prompts, echoes or messages, which messages mean "your input was rejected", whether a prompt accepts spaces, and hints that help the LLM correct a rejected input.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.NewLines(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String})
member.summary: The lines of that were not yet in , where both are the last N lines of the command-line history (oldest first) read before and after an input. The last line of may have grown in place (the prompt plus the typed input); it is then returned as the first new line. When the two snapshots do not overlap at all, every line of is new.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.Chronological(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},System.String)
member.summary: Puts a command-line history snapshot into chronological order (oldest first). AutoCAD 2027's Internal.Utils.GetLastCommandLines returns the NEWEST line first (seen in the first real run: the history read after DIMSCALE, DIMLUNIT, DIMDEC, DIMFRAC, DIMZIN listed DIMZIN first). The order is checked against (LASTPROMPT, the current line): when the last line is the current one the snapshot is already oldest first; when the first line is, it is reversed; when neither matches, the observed newest-first order is assumed.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.IsSystemNotice(System.String)
member.summary: True when is a notice of AutoCAD's system-variable monitor (SYSMON / SYSVARMONITOR): "**** System Variable Changed ****", "**** No System Variable Changed ****", "3 of the monitored system variables have changed from the preferred value. Use SYSVARMONITOR command to view changes." They are informational and never mean that an input was rejected.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.IsSettled(System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: True when AutoCAD has finished reacting to an input: it reacted at all (), the last poll brought no new events (), nothing typed is still queued, and it is either back at the Command prompt or showing a NEW prompt (a line ending in ':'). The echo of the input just typed ("Specify included angle: -90") is not a prompt: AutoCAD is still working on that input.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.IsWaitingForInput(System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: True when a command is really waiting for more input: it is active and the current line is a prompt. An active command whose current line still shows the echo of the last input is busy processing it, not waiting.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.Clean(System.String)
member.summary: Whitespace-normalised, trimmed text of a command-line line (null-safe).

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.IsPrompt(System.String)
member.summary: True when is a prompt waiting for input: it ends with ':' ("Specify next point or [Undo]:", "Select objects:", "Command:").

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.IsCommandPrompt(System.String)
member.summary: True when is the idle "Command:" prompt.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.FindRejection(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: The message in that says AutoCAD rejected the input ("Invalid point.", "Point or option keyword required.", "Requires numeric distance or two points.", "Unknown command ...", "... not found."), or null when there is none. Prompts and echoes are skipped.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.ContainsCancel(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String})
member.summary: True when one of is AutoCAD's cancel mark ("*Cancel*").

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.Messages(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.String},System.String)
member.summary: The informative messages among : not prompts, not the echo of the input typed at , not empty ("1 found", "Current settings: Offset distance = 9\"", "Invalid point.").

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.IsTextPrompt(System.String)
member.summary: True when is one of AutoCAD's text prompts, where spaces are part of the answer: "Enter text:", "MText:", "Enter attribute prompt:", "Enter default attribute value:", "Enter new attribute value:", "Enter new string:", "Enter string to change:", "Enter new text <...>:". At any other prompt a space acts like Enter, so an input with spaces is split into several answers.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.HasSeparator(System.String)
member.summary: True when typing at a prompt that does not take text would split it into several answers: it contains a space, a tab or a ';'.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandLineText.HintForRejection(System.String,System.String,System.String,AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.DrawingUnits)
member.summary: A short hint that helps correct a rejected input, or null: feet-inch input in a drawing that does not accept it, a bare number at a point prompt (AutoCAD then uses the mouse direction), an unknown option keyword, etc.

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandDecision.Blocked
member.summary: Never typed (other programs, program code, AutoLISP, opening/closing files, dialog-only commands...).

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict
member.summary: The policy decision for a command or an input, with a human-readable reason.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.Decision
member.summary: The decision.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.Subject
member.summary: What the decision is about: the canonical command name ("SHELL", "ERASE") or a short input description.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.Reason
member.summary: Why, in plain words ("runs another program..."); null when allowed.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.IsAllowed
member.summary: True when allowed.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.IsBlocked
member.summary: True when blocked.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.NeedsApproval
member.summary: True when the user must approve it first.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandVerdict.Describe
member.summary: "SHELL: runs another program..." (or just the subject when allowed).

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand
member.summary: A command as typed, split into prefixes and name, with its alias resolved.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.Typed
member.summary: The command as given, trimmed ("_.LA").

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.Prefix
member.summary: Leading prefix characters other than '-' ("_.", "'", "+"), in their original order.

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.Dash
member.summary: True when a '-' was among the leading characters (the command-line version of a command).

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.Name
member.summary: The name as typed, upper case, without prefixes ("LA").

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.Canonical
member.summary: The command the name stands for after alias resolution, without '-' ("LAYER").

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.CanonicalDash
member.summary: True when the resolved command is the command-line ('-') version ("-LA" or "LO" -> "-LAYOUT").

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.Transparent
member.summary: True when the command was typed transparently (with a leading apostrophe).

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.ParsedCommand.IsWellFormed
member.summary: True when is a well-formed AutoCAD command name.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy
member.summary:
Pure command policy for run_commands (no AutoCAD references). Every step's command and every input is checked BEFORE anything is typed:
Blocked (never typed): SHELL/SH and the operating-system commands of acad.pgp, APPLOAD, NETLOAD, ARX, VBA*, ACTIVEX*, SCRIPT, VLISP, WEBLOAD, CUI/menu loading, QUIT, EXIT, CLOSE, CLOSEALL, OPEN, NEW, QNEW, RECOVER and other file-opening commands, UNDO/U (the copilot has its own undo tool), security system variables, dialog-only commands with no command-line version, and any command or input starting with "(" or "!" (AutoLISP).
Needs approval: SAVE, QSAVE, SAVEAS, WBLOCK, EXPORT*, PLOT, PUBLISH, PURGE, LAYDEL, LAYMRG, AUDIT, other file writers, and ERASE (or CUTCLIP) with the selection keyword ALL.
Names are normalised first (leading _ . - + and the transparent ' stripped, upper case) and aliases resolved (built-in default acad.pgp aliases plus the user's acad.pgp when given).

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.NormalizeName(System.String)
member.summary: The normalised command name: trimmed, leading _ . - + and ' stripped, upper case ("_.-layer" -> "LAYER", "'ZOOM" -> "ZOOM"). Empty for null or blank input.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.IsAutoLisp(System.String)
member.summary: True when starts (after leading spaces) with "(" or "!", i.e. would be evaluated as AutoLISP.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.IsCommandNameText(System.String)
member.summary: True when (without prefixes) looks like an AutoCAD command name: a letter or digit followed by letters, digits, _ - or $ (at most 64 characters).

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.Parse(System.String,AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
member.summary: Splits into prefixes and name and resolves aliases.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.ClassifyCommand(System.String,AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
member.summary: Classifies a step's command (as typed, with prefixes). A dialog command that has a command-line version is Blocked here with a hint; gives the version to type instead.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.ClassifyInput(System.String,AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.CheckStep(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
member.summary: Every policy finding of a step (command and inputs) that is not Allowed, most severe first; empty when the whole step is allowed. Adds the ERASE ALL rule: ERASE or CUTCLIP with an input "ALL" needs approval.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.ClassifyStep(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.String},AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
member.summary: The most severe verdict for a whole step (Allowed when finds nothing).

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.CommandLineVersion(System.String,AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
member.summary: The command-line version to type instead of a dialog or palette command, keeping the other prefixes: "LAYER" -> "-LAYER", "_.LA" -> "_.-LAYER", "BH" -> "-HATCH", "MTEXT" -> "-MTEXT". Null when the command has no such version or is already the command-line version.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.IsSelectAll(System.String)
member.summary: True when an input is the selection keyword ALL ("ALL", "_ALL", case-insensitive).

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.ClassifyRunningCommand(System.String,AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandAliases)
member.summary: Classifies a command AutoCAD is about to run while a copilot call is in progress (the global command name of DocumentCollection.DocumentLockModeChanged, which may carry a leading '#' or other prefixes), on the security rules only: Blocked for other programs, program code, opening/closing files and security settings; NeedsApproval for the approval commands; Allowed otherwise. Dialog rules and session-only blocks (UNDO, U, MULTIPLE...) are ignored, because AutoCAD and running commands invoke such commands internally and the copilot's undo group uses UNDO.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandPolicy.CommandNamePattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[A-Z0-9][A-Z0-9_\\-$]*$
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [0-9A-Za-z\u212A].
○ Match a character in the set [$\-0-9A-Z_a-z\u212A] atomically any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandTables
member.summary: The data behind : which AutoCAD commands are never typed, which need the user's approval, which open dialog boxes or palettes (and their command-line versions), and the aliases of the default acad.pgp that map to any of them. Names are canonical, upper case, without prefixes.

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandTables.Blocked
member.summary: Commands that are never typed, with the reason shown to the LLM.

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandTables.NotVetoedWhileRunning
member.summary: Blocked commands that are refused only when the copilot is asked to type them, not vetoed when AutoCAD runs them while a call is in progress: the copilot's own undo group uses UNDO, and AutoCAD or a running command may invoke these internally. Everything else in (other programs, code, files, security) is also vetoed at run time.

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandTables.BlockedPrefixes
member.summary: Command name prefixes that are never typed (VBAIDE, VBARUN, ACTIVEX...).

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandTables.ProtectedSystemVariables
member.summary: System variables the copilot never changes (as SETVAR input or typed directly).

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.CommandTables.NeedsApproval

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.DraftingPace
member.summary:
How fast the copilot types AutoCAD commands (process-wide, thread-safe).
Watch mode (the default) pauses between typed inputs () and before each new command () so the user can follow every command and number in the command line and see the objects appear one by one. Fast mode ( = false) types without pauses; AutoCAD still finishes each input before the next one is typed.
The panel binds its Watch/Fast switch to ; the drafting engine reads the delays before every pause, so a change applies to the very next input, also in the middle of a running call. is raised on the thread that changed the mode (any thread) after the new value is visible, and only when the value really changed; handlers that touch WPF must marshal to the dispatcher themselves.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Drafting.InputRepair
member.summary:
The pure rules of run_commands' self-healing: safe, syntax-only repairs of inputs that AutoCAD rejected (or that the copilot would have to refuse), and the "finish" prompts where a forgotten trailing Enter may be pressed. The plug-in's drafting engine applies them while typing and reports every applied fix ("auto-fixed: ...").
Rules (each one only rewrites HOW a value is written, never WHAT it is):
: typographic minus signs and quote marks become ASCII ("−90" -> "-90", "12′6″" -> "12'6\""); spaces around ',' '<' '@' in coordinates are removed ("10, 20" -> "10,20"); two or three plain numbers separated by spaces at a point prompt become a coordinate ("10 20" -> "10,20"); a feet-inch length with a space ("6 1/2\"") is written without one ("6-1/2\"").
: lengths in feet-inches or with a unit (mm, cm, m, ft, in) that the drawing's LUNITS does not take are converted to drawing units when INSUNITS gives the scale (never when bare numbers in the same coordinate would become ambiguous); a degree sign or "deg" is removed from angles (AUNITS 0); an option keyword with a typo, a lower-case letter that is not its capital, or brackets/quotes is typed as the keyword's capital letters when exactly one option of the prompt fits.
: prompts where Enter only ends the command or selection (LINE/PLINE "Specify next point", "Select objects:", TEXT "Enter text:", -HATCH "Specify internal point", TRIM/EXTEND, "<Exit>" defaults, -LAYER/-LINETYPE main prompt, DIMCONTINUE/DIMBASELINE).
: the command-line version to retry when a command still opened a dialog box.
Nothing is fixed at text prompts (TEXT's "Enter text:", attribute values): there every character is meant literally.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Interaction.ICopilotUi
member.summary:
What the chat panel (its view model) provides to the backend for things that come from the add-in side rather than from the CLI's output stream: clarifying questions (ask_user), the task checklist (update_plan) and approvals for destructive tools.
Implemented by the panel's view model (ChatViewModel) and attached with ICopilotBackend.AttachUi. All members are called from background threads: implementations must marshal to the WPF dispatcher themselves and must never block the calling thread waiting for the UI thread synchronously (AutoCAD's main thread is the WPF thread).

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Learning.CopilotActivity
member.summary: Knows when the copilot itself works in AutoCAD (a tool call that types commands, switches drawings or changes the drawing), so the "Learn from me" recorder never mistakes the AI's work for the user's. The plug-in opens a scope with around every such tool call; stays true for a short tail after the last scope ends, because AutoCAD reports the end of a typed command (or the copilot's own Esc) slightly later. Thread-safe.

member.remarks:
Pattern:
\\s*\\((\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2})\\)\\s*$
Explanation:
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match '('.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit exactly 4 times.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match a Unicode digit exactly 2 times.
○ Match '-'.
○ Match a Unicode digit exactly 2 times.
○ Match ')'.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily any number of times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Learning.KnowledgeStore
member.summary: The local knowledge base the AI reads every turn and writes to (no model can be retrained: this is how the copilot "learns"): %LOCALAPPDATA%\AcadCopilot\knowledge\ with rules.md, style.md, lessons.md and recipes\<name>.md, all plain Markdown the user can open and edit. Writes are small, deduplicated (the newest item on the same subject wins), capped in size, atomic (temp file + rename) and serialised across processes (every chat tab runs its own MCP bridge) with a named mutex.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Learning.UserRecording
member.summary: One "Learn from me" recording: the user's own commands (with what they typed at each prompt and the objects each created, modified or erased), current-layer changes and drawing switches, in time order. Pure and AutoCAD-free: the plug-in feeds it from AutoCAD's events and says for every event whether the copilot caused it (then it is ignored). Memory is capped: at most actions are kept in detail, later ones are only counted by name. Pausing stops capturing without losing anything. Not thread-safe (AutoCAD's main thread only); the panel reads the counters from the same thread.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.AcadTurnQueue
member.summary: AutoCAD has one command line, so actions that type into it (run_commands, undo, cancel_command, and reads that have to switch the active drawing first) take turns: first come, first served, one at a time. Chats keep thinking and planning in parallel; only their drawing actions wait here. Cancelling a waiting entry removes it from the queue at once (Stop in that chat). Thread-safe; contains no AutoCAD code.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.ConversationJournal.DescribeContext(System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: The compact context block for another AI: earlier conversation (approved plan tables are in there), the task list, what the current job did so far and the last drawing facts. At most about 9,000 characters.
member.param: Include the current job's tool calls and its messages after the request (a switch in the middle of a job; the request itself is given separately).
Without : also list the current job's messages (a review), or only what came before it (false: a new provider gets the user's new message separately).

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.CopilotBackend
member.summary:
The panel backend: owns the runners, settings, sign-in, the AutoCAD host info, the chat sessions (one per tab, ), the limit on chats running at once and the in which the chats' drawing actions take turns. Also routes the add-in-side calls (questions, plans, approvals) to the session they belong to.
For compatibility it still implements itself: those members act on (the active tab, else the first one, created on demand).
Contains no AutoCAD code, so it is unit-tested directly.

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.CopilotBackend.StatusProbeTimeout
member.summary: Longest wait for one provider's status while choosing who takes over a job or reviews.

member.name: F:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.CopilotBackend.DefaultMaxRunningSessions
member.summary: Default for the most chats that may run at once (each runs its own CLI process; RAM is limited).
Creates the backend.
member.param: Builds the bridge launch info for each turn (each session adds its --session id).
The drawing that is active now, for binding a new session (called on the thread that creates the session; null = sessions start unbound and bind on their first tool call).
The most sessions that may run a turn at once.

The knowledge folder whose "WHAT YOU HAVE LEARNED" digest is added to every turn's instructions (defaults to , or to the "knowledge" folder next to when that is given, so tests never read the user's real knowledge).

member.name: P:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.ICopilotAssist.EmitNoticesAsText
member.summary: When true (default) the session also writes each / as a plain assistant message (TextDone), for chat views that do not render those events. A view that shows them itself (switch notice, review card) sets this to false.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Panel.ICopilotAssist.ReviewAsync(System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken)
member.summary: Runs a second-opinion review of this chat's drawing as a turn of its own: a separate CLI call (another signed-in provider when there is one, else the chat's provider in a fresh session) whose AutoCAD bridge is read-only. Streams the reviewer's tool activity, then , then exactly one TurnCompleted / TurnFailed.

member.summary:
One chat tab (): owns its per-provider CLI session ids, provider and model choice, the attached tab UI, the "always approve" memory, the running turn and a of the conversation. Created by ; the backend holds what is shared (runners, settings, sign-in, the AutoCAD turn queue, the running-turn limit, the feature switches).
A turn may continue with another provider (AI switching, ), may end with an automatic second-opinion review (), and "review this plan" runs the review (). Contains no AutoCAD code.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Presentation.PresentationPixels
member.summary: Pixel maths of export_view_png (pure, no GDI or AutoCAD types). AutoCAD's off-screen renderer draws on black, where colour 7 (white/black) is white. A presentation picture needs paper white with dark linework but the fills in their exact true colours, so the drawing is rendered twice on black: once only the colour fills (hatches, images), once only the linework, and lays the linework, darkened like ink, over the fills on white paper. Buffers hold height rows of stride bytes, pixels of 3 (B, G, R) or 4 (B, G, R, A) bytes.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Recovery.CheckpointCatalog
member.summary: The checkpoints of ONE open drawing in this AutoCAD session and the stack of AutoCAD UNDO marks the copilot placed for them. Pure bookkeeping (the plug-in types the UNDO commands): it knows, for a restore, how many UNDO Back commands reach a checkpoint and which fingerprint the drawing must show after each, so a Back that lands somewhere else (the user undid past a mark, placed own marks, or the drawing was reopened) is detected and reversed with REDO. Not thread-safe: used on AutoCAD's main thread.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Recovery.CheckpointStore
member.summary: The checkpoint copies on disk: %LOCALAPPDATA%\AcadCopilot\checkpoints\<drawing key>\ holds one DWG per checkpoint (written by the plug-in with Database.Wblock + SaveAs, never the user's own file) and index.json (name, file, time, fingerprint, drawing path). member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Services.SymbolLibraryDxf
member.summary: Writes the services symbol library as an AutoCAD R12 DXF (AC1009): every symbol as a BLOCK (geometry on layer 0, colour BYBLOCK, ATTDEF for its label) plus a catalogue sheet in ENTITIES (one INSERT with its ATTRIB per symbol, the symbol's name and title, and the draft notes) on the services layers. R12 is chosen on purpose: it needs no handles, owners or OBJECTS section, so a file written without AutoCAD is still read reliably by AutoCAD's DXFIN / Database.DxfIn. Plain ASCII, CRLF line ends, invariant numbers. Validate with .

Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:

○ Match a character in the set [^;\\{}] atomically any number of times.
○ Match ';'.

member.remarks:
Pattern:
^(SEE|REFER|REF\\.?|NOTE|NOTES|AS PER)\\b|[=]
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions, atomically.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 4 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "SEE".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "REF".
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "ER".
○ Match '.' greedily, optionally.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "NOTE".
○ Match 'S' lazily, optionally.
○ Match the string "AS PER".
○ Match if at a word boundary.
○ Match '='.

Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:

○ Match the string "LOCATION".
○ Match the string "KEY".
○ Match a whitespace character atomically at least once.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match with 2 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "PLAN".
○ Match the string "LAYOUT".
○ Match if at a word boundary.

Pattern:
^(MD|SD\\d*|D\\d{0,2}|W\\d{0,2}|KW\\d*|V\\d{0,2})$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match with 6 alternative expressions.
○ Match the string "MD".
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "SD".
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically any number of times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match 'D'.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at most 2 times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match 'W'.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at most 2 times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match the string "KW".
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically any number of times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match 'V'.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at most 2 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.

member.name: T:AcadCopilot.Core.Sheets.ModelArrangement
member.summary: Lines the drawings of model space up the professional way: the floor plans in one row (ground, first, second ..., terrace) with the same spacing between their wall extents, so walls and stairs line up from floor to floor; the elevations in a row below (front first, under the ground floor plan), then the sections and the site plan; anything else in a third row. The gap between drawings is about one plan width (at least 20'). The first floor plan (or the first drawing) stays where it is. Pure.

Pattern:
\\(\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*[_ ]?x[_ ]?\\s*(\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)?)\\s*[_ ]?\\s*(MM|Inches|in)\\s*\\)
Options:
RegexOptions.IgnoreCase | RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match '('.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ 1st capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily any number of times.
○ Match a character in the set [ _] atomically, optionally.
○ Match a character in the set [Xx].
○ Match a character in the set [ _] greedily, optionally.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ 2nd capture group.
○ Match a Unicode digit greedily at least once.
○ Optional (greedy).
○ Match '.'.
○ Match a Unicode digit atomically at least once.
○ Match a whitespace character greedily any number of times.
○ Match a character in the set [ _] greedily, optionally.
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ 3rd capture group.
○ Match with 3 alternative expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Mm] exactly 2 times.
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match a character in the set [Nn].
○ Match a character in the set [Cc].
○ Match a character in the set [Hh].
○ Match a character in the set [Ee].
○ Match a character in the set [Ss].
○ Match a sequence of expressions.
○ Match a character in the set [Ii].
○ Match a character in the set [Nn].
○ Match a whitespace character atomically any number of times.
○ Match ')'.

member.name: M:AcadCopilot.Core.Tools.ToolDefinition.NamePattern
member.remarks:
Pattern:
^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,63}$
Options:
RegexOptions.CultureInvariant
Explanation:
○ Match if at the beginning of the string.
○ Match a character in the set [a-z].
○ Match a character in the set [0-9_a-z] atomically at least 1 and at most 63 times.
○ Match if at the end of the string or if before an ending newline.
